system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General warranty cap is 20% of price ($4.8m). | Higher cap, ideally 30–50%, with separate uncapped/carve-out regimes. | **Reject as sole regime; seek ≥30% general cap.** A $4.8m cap may be inadequate against identified operational and contractual exposures. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | $25k de minimis; $250k deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis and basket; preferably tipping basket, or a lower deductible basket. | **Negotiate to $10k–$15k de minimis and $100k–$150k basket, preferably tipping.** The proposed thresholds could leave meaningful aggregated losses unrecovered. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months; Seller seeks all-claims application unless expressly excluded. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with longer distinct periods for tax, IP, fundamental matters and specific indemnities. | **Reject universal 18-month period; seek 24 months minimum.** The seller’s wording risks prematurely extinguishing claims whose consequences emerge later. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limits. | Separate fundamental regime: 100% of price cap and longer period (at least 6 years), with title preferably uncapped. | **Reject.** Ownership and power to sell are core deal risks and should not be constrained by the ordinary warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out. | Express preservation of claims for fraud, fraudulent concealment and deliberate/wilful misconduct; no cap, threshold or time-bar to the extent legally permissible. | **Insert an express fraud carve-out.** “All claims” language may improperly seek to limit recourse for dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Broad general disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail to identify nature and consequences; no data-room/public-records sweep-up. | **Reject general disclosure.** A bulk disclosure shifts diligence risk to Buyer and can qualify warranties without clear notice. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers, including matters discoverable in data room or public records. | No constructive-knowledge/discoverability bar; at most, a narrow actual knowledge qualifier of named Buyer deal-team members, excluding advisers. | **Delete, or limit tightly to actual knowledge of specified individuals.** “Discoverable” knowledge recreates the unacceptable broad disclosure defence. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; treats condition as satisfied upon written consent. Final consent and satisfaction of its conditions are not evidenced. | Consent, including all conditions, as a Completion condition or a Buyer-controlled waiver right; meaningful long-stop/termination protection. | **Make complete Bluefen consent a CP and require evidence of compliance with all conditions.** Bluefen represents about $3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately $3.2m remains outstanding; release is to be provided after Completion. | Repayment and unconditional discharge/release of all debt and security at or before Completion, funded from Seller proceeds; escrow/holdback if needed. | **Reject post-Completion release.** Buyer must acquire a debt-free, cash-free target free of Riverlark security at Completion. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | $420k conditional completion bonuses excluded from funds flow; on-costs unstated. | Seller-funded payment or a dollar-for-dollar purchase-price reduction/Completion adjustment, including payroll tax, super and all on-costs; clear retention allocation. | **Require a specific price adjustment or Seller payment/indemnity.** These Completion-linked liabilities should not become Buyer’s unpriced cost. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; $180k remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is available. | Broad specific indemnity for ownership, use, infringement and remediation; payment evidence and assignment/confirmation before Completion. | **Expand indemnity and make IP evidence a Completion deliverable.** Non-payment may prevent transfer of project materials essential to the business. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls it preliminary and non-material; no confirmed access, scope or notification assessment. | Completion investigation, preservation and disclosure of evidence, risk assessment, remediation/notification plan, and a specific indemnity/holdback. | **Do not accept “non-material” characterisation; obtain a specific indemnity and completion protections.** Potential exposure concerns approximately 1,240 personal-data records and may crystallise after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total $330k; characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Details of commitments, termination rights, accruals and authority; protection against undisclosed/non-ordinary commitments and, if applicable, price adjustment. | **Require full contract analysis and covenant/indemnity protection if non-ordinary or unavoidable.** The disclosure does not establish whether the costs are avoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks limitations, remedies and time limits applying to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, restrictive covenants and fraud. | **Insert a clear category hierarchy and carve-outs.** A universal limitations clause can unintentionally cap or time-bar risks negotiated separately. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on company share register (DD-012) showing Seller holds 100%; says Buyer must undertake its own verification. | Completion deliverables confirming valid title, no encumbrances/options/security interests, duly executed transfers, updated register and director resolutions; PPSR and corporate searches. | **Require independent verification and robust title deliverables.** A register alone does not establish absence of encumbrances or competing interests. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranties settled under general cap/time-limit regime. | Separate, tailored tax covenant/indemnity with extended limitation period; IP warranties and indemnity with separate higher/uncapped protection as appropriate. | **Reject treatment under the general regime.** Historic tax and IP ownership/infringement liabilities can be substantial and emerge beyond an 18-month general period. |
=== END ADVICE ===
